label: provisional
paradigm: These criteria serve a buyer choosing what to purchase, new or pre-owned: an evidence-based, value-aware buyer who wants an informed view of history and context. They are one reasonable buyer's stance, not the only one, and this version is provisional: drafted from published sources, not yet compiled or ratified.

change_log.reason: Drafted from ISO 6425:2018 as summarised by Fratello and Time+Tide (the standard itself is paywalled and was not read), brand water-resistance guidance (Timex), enthusiast press and the Teddy content audit of 2026-11-14.

spec_fields.water_resistance_m: number: rated water resistance in metres
spec_fields.bezel: lower-case string describing the bezel or diving-time indicator, for example "unidirectional 60-minute ceramic" or "digital"
spec_fields.crown: lower-case string describing the crown, for example "screw-down"

wearer.statement: What the buyer will actually do in the water (desk diver, swimming and snorkelling, recreational scuba, saturation) sets the rating and features worth paying for.
The watch fits the buyer's wrist: lug-to-lug length inside the flat top of the wrist and a thickness the buyer's cuffs and comfort allow. Measure these rather than trusting the stated diameter.
wearer.test: Compare the stated lug-to-lug length with the buyer's measured flat wrist width; try the watch on where possible.

watch.statement: Water resistance of at least 100 m, the ISO 6425 minimum for a divers' watch.

200 m or more, the rating many enthusiasts treat as the floor for a proper dive watch and brands list for recreational scuba. This is practitioner consensus, not the standard: the standard asks for 100 m.

A diving-time indicator protected against inadvertent handling, with minute resolution over 60 minutes (ISO 6425 allows a rotating bezel, a digital display or other). A unidirectional rotating bezel is the usual way to meet it; record a digital indicator in the bezel field as 'digital'. Any other indicator is judged by hand.
A screw-down (or otherwise locking) crown, so the crown cannot be left open by accident. A push-pull crown does not disqualify a watch from recreational use.
Time, diving time, five-minute markings and a running indicator readable at 25 cm in darkness (ISO 6425's visibility test), so lume on hands, indices, bezel and the seconds hand.
Survives the ISO 6425 magnetic test (4,800 A/m, keeping accuracy within 30 s/day of its pre-test rate) and shock test. Usually stated by the brand only when the watch is certified.
A strap or bracelet that survives salt water (rubber, textile or metal, not leather) and a diver's extension or adjustable clasp to fit over a wetsuit.
